objective: Proof and verification. Encode the solutions of a plane knot space minus a line as integer potentials of line-face matchings (flip counts, the hole at zero), which form an L-natural-convex set; show that the gluing line's three states form a staircase in the port potentials; and derive the access lemma by midpoint rounding: a pinning never selects the pattern whose odd port is tied to the hub, and with no port tied the two-port near knot points one step from the pinned pattern. Verify each ingredient on plane spaces.
status: Proved by PLANAR-THEOREM-20261102-001A-P001: the access lemma is a theorem for plane knot spaces with Kasteleyn signs. Line-face matchings have integer potentials (the hole at zero) forming an L-natural convex set whose parities are the values relative to the hub; the gluing line's states form a staircase; rounded midpoints show that a pinning never selects the state of a hub-tied port and, with no port tied, that the hub and the non-odd ports form a near knot one step from the pinned pattern. With the route lemma: no pinned-and-separated three-point hub knot is new on a plane near side, for any far side
title: The access lemma, by discrete convexity
